papers.title: Motivic $C_p$-power operations in $\mathrm{MGL}$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give a new proof of the Hopkins-Morel-Hoyois theorem for fields $k$ of characteristic unequal to $p$ containing all primitive $p$-power roots of unity for a fixed prime $p$. This new proof follows Quillen's proof for the structure of the homotopy groups of $\mathrm{MU}$ which utilizes topological power operations. To this end we define a motivic analog of the Steenrod power operations, using the theory of normed motivic spectra as developed by Bachmann--Hoyois and their application for the definition of motivic colimits as developed by Bachmann-Elmanto-Heller.

papers.title: Computations in weight 3 of higher Bloch groups
papers.abstract: We computationally investigate a weight 3 analogue of the relationship between higher Bloch groups, algebraic K-theory, higher regulators, and special values of Dedekind zeta functions. In particular, for F a number field F, we define the pruned Bloch group B _3(F) and compare the covolume of its regulator lattice with zeta_F(3). We define a quantity kappa_3(F), which is conjecturally an integer, that is expected to be closely related to the order of K_4(O_F).

papers.title: Generic tensor products are not maximal
papers.abstract: We construct tensor products of uniform matroids which are strictly freer than their generic linear tensor products. In particular, the generic tensor product of two copies of $U_{7,9}$ is not maximal. More generally, for every $a,b\ge2$, this holds for $U_{7,a+7}$ and $U_{7,b+7}$. The construction disproves the uniform tensor-product formulation of Mason's conjecture. Its dual is a relaxation of an explicit circuit-hyperplane of a generic birigidity matroid. By the author's representability theorem, the resulting matroids are non-representable over every field. We also obtain full-rank counterexamples to the Jackson--Tanigawa hyperconnectivity conjecture in every dimension $d\ge2$.

papers.title: Sheaves on polynomials and polynomial sheaves
papers.abstract: We show that several Dold-Kan type equivalences can be understood as a passage from constructible sheaves on symmetric products (i.e. spaces of polynomials) to polynomial sheaves in the sense of Goodwillie-Weiss calculus, by means of a natural analytic expansion functor. This geometric perspective provides access to standard tools from sheaf theory such as the six functor formalism and $t$-structures. For example, the equivalence between filtered objects and coherent chain complexes in a stable $\infty$-category receives a geometric incarnation as Verdier duality between $!$-sheaves and $*$-cosheaves on an $\infty$-dimensional simplex. As a main application, we obtain an intrinsic geometric explanation for the appearance of vanishing cycle data for perverse sheaves in a paracyclic variant of the Dold--Kan correspondence pioneered by Dwyer and Kan, at the same time lifting their equivalence to stable $\infty$-categories.

papers.title: A minimising principle for interval covers of zigzag persistence modules
papers.abstract: Zigzag persistence modules serve as an essential tool in topological data analysis. The fundamental theorem of persistent homology states that any zigzag persistence module decomposes into a direct sum of simple building blocks called interval modules. We consider an interval cover, a possibly redundant family of interval submodules spanning every vertex space of a finite zigzag persistence module. We give an elementary descent argument that replaces a redundant cover with a minimal one that is an interval decomposition. This provides an optimisation perspective on persistence modules and their interval decomposition. As an application, we give an estimate of the generalised rank invariant in terms of a cover.

papers.title: Countable models of one-dimensional Peano continua
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that a one-dimensional Peano continuum $X$ admits a weak homotopy equivalence $X\to C$ to a countable space $C$ if and only if the wild set $\mathbf{w}(X)$ is countable.

papers.title: Homotopy operations on higher Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We determine the multiplicative structures of the homotopy operations on derived Lie algebras, derived restricted Lie algebras and partition Lie algebras, as well as the relation between these. Under Koszul duality, this follows from a calculation of the homotopy operations on derived rings, p-truncated algebras and divided power algebras over $\mathbb{F}_p$.

papers.title: Localization, cobordism, and twisted $\chi_y$-genera of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$
papers.abstract: We use the method of equivariant localization to obtain a recursion for the cobordism-valued one-point psi-class intersections on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$, and hence the cobordism classes $[\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}]$. Restricting to the hyperbolic formal group law, we recover the Poincar\'{e} polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ as a special case, and obtain new formulas for Hirzebruch $\chi_y$-genera of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ twisted by tautological line bundles.

papers.title: Morse-Maxwell Theory for Directed Acyclic Graph
papers.abstract: The Maxwell graph of a directed acyclic graph is obtained from its iterated basin and hill boundaries. The unweighted counts of extrema at these levels need not satisfy Morse inequalities. We assign multiplicities by the reduced homology of lower and upper order links and retain the vertices with nonzero local homology. The resulting graph preserves both boundary hierarchies, the local groups, and the homology of all sublevel and superlevel order complexes. Its descending and ascending Morse numbers satisfy the weak and strong Morse inequalities over any field. We also construct a Morse chain complex and compute the local groups in several examples. Finally, we consider homology on the original Maxwell graph and prove analogous inequalities for path homology using relative local groups.

papers.title: Topology of rational equivalence closures and Lawson homology
papers.abstract: Rational equivalence need not be closed in the Chow topology, and its closure can have infinitely generated homotopy groups. For a connected reduced complex projective variety, we prove that this closure is locally contractible and that its quotient in the algebraically trivial cycles is a finite or countable weak product of circles. The quotient map admits a global continuous section. Consequently, the higher homotopy of the cycle space is carried by the closure and is canonically identified with Lawson homology. We describe the remaining fundamental group quotient and its integral Walker comparison. Applications include smooth projective examples with infinite rank closure homotopy throughout prescribed finite intervals and a family of abelian threefolds with four simultaneously dense, nonconstructible quotient rank strata.

papers.title: BV structure on the Hochschild cohomology of Liu-Schulz algebras in characteristic two
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $2$, let $\rho\in K^\times$, and let $R_\rho$ be the corresponding Liu-Schulz algebra. We give a complete description of the Gerstenhaber bracket and the BV structure on the Hochschild cohomology ring $\operatorname{HH}^*(R_\rho)$.

papers.title: A nilpotent version of the first Kac conjecture
papers.abstract: We derive a formula for the nilpotent Kac polynomial and define an explicit generalized Kac-Moody Lie algebra (by generators and relations) and conjecture that its graded dimensions recover the constant terms of the nilpotent Kac polynomial. We outline empirical evidence supporting the conjecture and prove it for two special classes of quivers: quivers without oriented cycles except loops and quivers with "negative enough" Euler form.

papers.title: A vanishing-cycle obstruction to smoothing Calabi-Yau threefolds
papers.abstract: We prove a homological obstruction to smoothing projective Calabi-Yau threefolds with nodes and anticanonical cones over smooth del Pezzo surfaces of degrees six and seven. On a crepant resolution that is small over the nodes and blows up the cone vertices, any smoothing forces a relation among link classes bounding in the local Milnor fibers. The relation is nonzero at every node and degree-seven point, and at each degree-six point smoothed through the one-dimensional component. The proof uses vanishing periods and applies to smoothing arcs of arbitrary contact order, extending the necessity direction of Friedman's criterion. We apply the obstruction to a Batyrev hypersurface whose thirty singularities are individually smoothable but which admits no smoothing, even formally. On its mirror partner, two nodes cannot be smoothed by any analytic deformation, independently of a locally nonsmoothable cone point.

papers.title: All Strict Calabi--Yau Threefolds of Height One Lift to Characteristic 0
papers.abstract: We prove that every strict Calabi--Yau threefold of Artin--Mazur height one over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p>0 admits a projective lift to W(k). No assumption is made on the torsion in its crystalline cohomology, and p is arbitrary. Using the crystalline period map of Brantner and Taelman, we show that the obstruction to extending a lift over W_n(k) is the Bockstein of a torsion coordinate of its period point, and that this coordinate can always be made to vanish by varying the lift. The mixed-characteristic deformation functor need not be smooth: for a Calabi--Yau threefold of height one constructed by Addington and Bragg in characteristic 3, some lifts over W_2(k) do not extend over W_3(k). This disproves a conjecture of Achinger and Zdanowicz.

papers.title: Analytic q-inequalities and a proof of Bergeron's conjecture
papers.abstract: For integers $1\le a\le b\le c\le d$ with $ad=bc$, Bergeron asked whether the difference of Gaussian binomial coefficients $\binom{b+c}{b}_q-\binom{a+d}{a}_q$ has nonnegative coefficients. We prove that it does, and more generally that $\binom{b+c}{b}_q-\binom{a+d}{a}_q$ has nonnegative coefficients whenever $a\le b\le c$ and $ad\le bc$, a strengthening proposed by Troyka. The proof is analytic rather than bijective. We develop a toolkit for coefficientwise inequalities, including a coefficientwise local limit theorem for Gaussian polynomials based on Irwin--Hall densities, and use it in a Pascal-type induction that proves the case $a\le 20$. For general $a$ the problem reduces to a two-parameter inequality between linearly interpolated Gaussian polynomials. Near its base case this inequality reduces exactly to the monotonicity of rational $q$-Catalan numbers. Using the circle method with explicit error terms, we prove the conjecture of Chen, Wang and Wang that the coefficients of MacMahon's $q$-Catalan numbers $C_n(q)$ are unimodal for every $n\ge16$, and an analogue for the rational $q$-Catalan numbers $C_{x,N+1}(q)$ with $x\le N\le 2x$. Beyond this range the difference splits into two nonnegative parts, which we compare degree by degree using local limit bounds for Gaussian polynomials that are uniform in both parameters. The proof is computer-assisted: it uses exact integer and rational arithmetic, ball arithmetic, and one floating-point computation with a proved error bound. The scripts and the logs of their runs are provided as ancillary files.

papers.title: Asymptotics for number of indecomposable components of tensor powers of the natural $\mathrm{SL}_2$-module in odd characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic $p$, let $G= {\rm SL}_2(K)$, and let $V$ be the natural representation of $G$. Let $b_k$ denote the number of $G$-indecomposable factors of $V^{\otimes k}$, counted with multiplicity, and let $\delta_p=1-\log_{p^2}\!\bigl(\tfrac{p+1}{2}\bigr)$. Then there exists a smooth, strictly positive, multiplicatively $p^2$-periodic function $\omega(t)$ such that $b_k$ is asymptotic to $\omega(k)k^{-\delta_p}2^k$. We also show that $t^{-\delta}\omega(t)$ arises as the limiting density of renormalized convolutions of rescaled copies of a positive weight $3/2$ theta function, obtained from the boundary heat flux of the Dirichlet heat kernel on $(0,p)$.

papers.title: Automorphic functions for nilpotent extensions of curves over finite fields
papers.abstract: We define and study the subspace of cuspidal functions for $G$-bundles (and its ramified analogs) on a class of nilpotent extensions of curves over a finite field. In the case of length $2$ extensions and of $G=\mathrm{GL}_2$, we prove that the space of cuspidal functions (for bundles with a fixed determinant) is finite-dimensional and provide bounds on its dimension. In this case we also relate cuspidality to Hecke finiteness, defined in terms of the action of some natural Hecke operators. Finally, we construct some Hecke eigenfunctions using the relation to Higgs bundles over the corresponding reduced curve.

papers.title: Bethe Cycles, Frobenius Identities, and Quantum/Classical Duality
papers.abstract: We study Frobenius action on the trigonometric Ruijsenaars--Schneider system associated with cotangent bundles to complete flag varieties. The construction continues the program initiated by Etingof and Varchenko and developed in quantum $K$-theory by the author and Smirnov. We explain how the monodromy eigenvectors recently constructed by Tarasov and Varchenko fit the quantum/classical duality between Bethe equations and tRS level sets. At a root of unity, all partial shifts cancel in the Newton--Adams combinations of the tRS Hamiltonians, leaving precisely the operators obtained by Frobenius action. This proves compatibility of the joint eigenvalue problem with Frobenius action in every rank and at every root order.

papers.title: Beyond Endoscopy via Poisson Summation for GL(2,K)
papers.abstract: In the early 2000's, R. Langlands proposed a strategy called Beyond Endoscopy to attack the principle of functoriality, which is one of the central questions of present day mathematics. A first step was achieved by A. Altug who worked with the group $GL(2,\mathbb{Q})$ in a series of three papers. We generalize the first part of this result to a class of totally real number fields. In particular, we cancel the contribution of the trivial and special representations to the trace formula using an additive Poisson summation on the regular elliptic terms.

papers.title: Bridgeland stability and Gieseker stability I: Limit stability
papers.abstract:
We study the large volume limit of Bridgeland stability conditions on smooth projective varieties. For each fixed ray in a suitable angular sector, we prove that an object of $\mathrm{D}^b(X)$ is Bridgeland (semi)stable in the corresponding hearts for all sufficiently large radii if and only if it is a pure $H$-Gieseker (semi)stable sheaf. In this sector, we identify the category of coherent sheaves as the limiting heart in the sense of eventual membership. We also identify a perverse coherent limiting heart in the opposite angular sector.
  The key ingredients are uniform HN-phase estimates for bounded families of pure sheaves, coefficient bounds for the coherent images of potential destabilizers, and a criterion forcing narrow exact sequences in the varying hearts to be bounded saturated coherent sequences.

papers.title: Classification of vanishing fusion rings of rank four
papers.abstract: A fusion ring is said to be vanishing if one of its multiplication matrices has determinant zero. We classify all vanishing fusion rings of rank four. We then provide a more explicit classification in the integral case, which leads to new consequences: there are infinitely many nonisomorphic simple integral vanishing fusion rings of rank four and no simple integral fusion ring of rank four is 1-Frobenius. We also classify all Burnside fusion rings of rank four.

papers.title: Cluster type smooth Fano threefolds
papers.abstract: We prove that most rational smooth Fano threefolds are compactifications of $\mathbb{G}_m^3$. More precisely, we study which smooth Fano threefolds are cluster type, i.e., for which smooth Fano threefolds $X$ one can find a boundary $B\in |-K_X|$ and an embedding $\mathbb{G}_m^3\hookrightarrow X\setminus B$. We prove that many important classes of smooth Fano threefolds are cluster type. For instance, a smooth Fano threefold which is the blow-up of either $\mathbb{P}^3$ or $\mathbb{Q}^3$ and is general in its deformation space is of cluster type. As a consequence, we show that among the $105$ families parametrizing all smooth Fano threefolds, the general element of precisely $87$ families is of cluster type. We prove that a general prime smooth Fano threefold of genus $7$ is not of cluster type. This is the only family whose general element is rational but not of cluster type. Finally, we prove that cluster type projective klt varieties are cylindrical and we give a criterion for such a cylinder to be anticanonically polar. Using this, we reduce the cylindricity problem for smooth Fano threefolds to the families $\mathcal{N}^{\mathrm{o}}\,1.3$, $\mathcal{N}^{\mathrm{o}}\,1.5$, and $\mathcal{N}^{\mathrm{o}}\,1.6$.

papers.title: Combinatorial description of the mirabolic quantum Schur-Weyl duality
papers.abstract: We prove an explicit correspondence between the irreducible finite dimensional representations of the mirabolic quantum group $MU(n)$ and those of the mirabolic Hecke algebra $MH_d$ given by the mirabolic quantum Schur-Weyl duality. In particular, this resolves a generalization of a conjecture by the second author. The proof is via a careful analysis of the $MU(n)$-weight spaces and the eigenvalues of the Jucys Murphy elements of $MH_d$ on the mirabolic tensor space.

papers.title: Compact generation and perfect objects in homotopy categories of exact model structures
papers.abstract: Compact generation allows large triangulated categories to be studied through suitably small objects. For homotopy categories arising from exact model structures, a natural question is how this intrinsic notion of smallness relates to finite presentation in the underlying exact category. In this paper, we investigate this relation for hereditary projective model structures generated by finitely presented Gorenstein projective objects. We establish compact generation and study the stronger requirement that every compact object admits a finitely presented cofibrant representative. We call objects with such representatives perfect. Under local coherence and the existence of enough projectives among the finitely presented objects, the finitely presented cofibrant objects form a Frobenius category whose stable category describes the perfect objects and whose idempotent completion recovers all compact objects. The relative $Q$-shaped setting, for suitable small categories $Q$, makes explicit how these finiteness properties depend on the choice of exact structure. The pure exact structure yields a compactly generated homotopy category, called the $Q$-shaped pure derived category. On the other hand, the split exact structure yields the $Q$-shaped homotopy category, which is compactly generated only in the pure semisimple case, analogously to the classical homotopy category of complexes. Finally, for acyclic $Q$ and for left artinian rings, we show that every compact object admits a strictly perfect representative. In particular, we establish that compact and perfect objects coincide, proving the conjecture of Holm and Jorgensen under these hypotheses.

papers.title: Comparing classical tilting modules and $\tau$-tilting modules
papers.abstract: We characterize support $\tau$-tilting modules as classical tilting modules over quotient algebras satisfying a tensor-vanishing condition, and characterize classical tilting modules as $\tau$-tilting modules satisfying a ${\rm Tor}^1$-vanishing condition. We use delooping levels to study \emph{Self-orthogonal $\tau$-tilting Conjecture}: any self-orthogonal $\tau$-tilting module is classical tilting. We confirm the conjecture when the endomorphism algebra of the module has finite global delooping level.

papers.title: Counting the Fixed Points of Binary Belief Propagation: Generic Degree, Syzygies, and Real Solutions
papers.abstract: How many fixed points does belief propagation have on a binary pairwise model? Over complex parameters, the admissible equations of a finite loopless multigraph form an algebraic family whose generic degree we determine: it is a graph state sum over edge sets without vertices of degree one, each vertex of positive degree contributing one less than its degree. We give two geometric realizations of this state sum. The first is the total Betti number of a universal edge-incidence ring constructed without parameters. Its full graded Betti table is the state sum, its Tor algebra is natural for noncontracting graph maps, the alternating numerator recovers the graph polynomial of Watanabe and Fukumizu, and an Artin reduction by a regular sequence realizes the one-variable specialization, corrected for tree components. The second lies in the actual family: at the strong-field boundary each state factor is a ramification index, and at sufficiently strong field the state charts exhaust the admissible complex fiber. For fixed nonzero real couplings, every Eulerian message-sign sector contains a real fixed point at every external field, and strong fields attain this lower bound: one admissible real fixed point per element of the binary cycle space and one positive fixed point. For graphs of maximum degree at most three, this minimum equals the number of minimal module generators of the edge-incidence ring. One state decomposition connects the complex degree, graded syzygies, and an attained minimum real count. The degree, selected ring and resolution statements, and the real counts are formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: Critical Diameters and Vietoris-Rips Filtrations
papers.abstract:
We relate critical diameters of finite configurations to the topology of Vietoris-Rips complexes. For a compact metric space and $0<r<s$, we prove that the canonical inclusion from scale $r$ to scale $s$ is a homotopy equivalence whenever $[r,s)$ contains no diameter of a finite labelled configuration at which the diameter function has zero weak slope.
  On Riemannian manifolds, weak-slope stationarity implies Clarke criticality. At positive diameter, when the distances realizing the diameter are smooth, both are equivalent to first-order stationarity: the absence of a direction decreasing all these distances to first order. For closed connected smooth manifolds, the Clarke critical diameter spectrum has Hausdorff dimension zero, even at the cut locus. In the real-analytic case, it is finite at each fixed number of labels and countable over all label numbers.
  On the unit round sphere $S^m$, $m\geq1$, positive nonantipodal weak-slope stationary configurations are characterized by nonzero nonnegative equilibrium stresses. The least positive critical diameter is $\arccos(-1/(m+1))$, and the first accumulation point is $\arccos(-1/m)$. We lift every such stress through a spherical stack construction adapted from Lov\'asz, producing stationary diameters that approach the original value from below in the next dimension as the number of layers increases. We also give example in general metric space showing that weak-slope stationary diameters need not correspond to changes in the homotopy type of Vietoris-Rips complexes.

papers.title: Decompositions of birational toric morphism between threefolds
papers.abstract: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a birational morphism between smooth projective threefolds, Koll\'ar asked that if $f$ could be decomposed into smooth blow-downs and smooth flops. In this paper we show that the toric version is true.

papers.title: Deformation of nef adjoint canonical line bundles
papers.abstract:
Much inspired by J. A. Wi\'sniewski's nef-value function method, we prove that in a smooth projective family over the unit disk, if the adjoint bundle of the canonical line bundle with a relatively semiample line bundle is nef on one fiber, then it remains nef on all fibers. We further extend this result to the semiampleness of the adjoint canonical line bundles. Using these, we prove the deformation invariance of any generalized plurigenera by assuming that only one fiber admits the semiample canonical line bundle and improve the first author--Xiao-Lei Liu's recent deformation rigidity of projective manifolds with semiample canonical line bundles. In particular, also by E. Viehweg--K. Zuo's result on the minimal number of singular fibers in a family and the first author--X. Liu's isotriviality result, if a projective family over $\mathbb{P}^1$ or an elliptic curve has one fiber with the big and nef (or more generally semiample) canonical line bundle, then all fibers are isomorphic to this fiber.
  Next, much inspired by M. Andreatta--T. Peternell's deformation theoretical approach, we prove that, in a smooth K\"ahler family of threefolds, if the canonical line bundle of one fiber is not nef, then none of its small deformations admits a nef canonical line bundle either. This partially confirms a problem posed by F. Campana--T. Peternell and the global stability of semiampleness of canonical line bundles of threefolds under a K\"ahler smooth deformation.

papers.title: Delooping levels on Morita context algebras
papers.abstract: We study the behavior of various delooping levels in the setting of Morita context algebras with zero bimodule homomorphisms. Building on the notion of syzygies for modules over such algebras, we establish conditions under which the delooping level (see [6]) of a Morita context algebra is finite, provided that the component algebras also have finite delooping levels. We further extend these results to other invariants, the global delooping level (see [2]) and the derived delooping level (see [8]), showing how their finiteness is preserved in the Morita context. Several examples illustrate both the applicability of our criteria and the necessity of the hypotheses, highlighting cases where the delooping level of the whole algebra can be smaller than that of its components.

papers.title: Derived categories of log del Pezzo surfaces with $\frac13(1,1)$ singularities
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a log del Pezzo surface with only $\frac13(1,1)$ singularities. We compare the derived categories of its minimal resolution, canonical stack, and singular surface. For every family in the Corti--Heuberger classification, Orlov's blow-up formula and the Ishii--Ueda correspondence give explicit full exceptional collections on the canonical stacks, of length $12-K_X^2+\frac{4k}{3}$ when $X$ has $k$ singular points. In the one-point index-one cascade, the canonical stacks are blow-ups of the weighted projective stack $\mathbb P(1,1,3)$ at distinct smooth points and admit explicit full strong exceptional collections of line bundles. For quasismooth hypersurfaces $X_{10}\subset\mathbb P(1,2,3,5)$, we construct a full strong exceptional collection of $13$ objects with an explicitly computed Euler matrix. The exceptional lattice determines the Brauer group: $\mathrm{Br}(X)=0$ for $k\leq5$, while $\mathrm{Br}(X)\cong\mathbb Z/3$ for $k=6$. We construct semiorthogonal decompositions of $D^b(\mathrm{coh}\,X)$ for the one- and three-point cascades and of a Brauer-twisted derived category for the six-point cascade.

papers.title: Duflo--Serganova functor for chiral differential operators on classical invariant rings
papers.abstract: We study the Duflo--Serganova functor for vertex algebras of chiral differential operators on classical invariant rings, introduced in \cite{ADS}. Our main result is a general cancellation theorem showing that a common bosonic and fermionic summand can be removed by Duflo--Serganova reduction. We apply this theorem to obtain Duflo--Serganova reduction isomorphisms for two families of simple orthosymplectic affine vertex superalgebras at levels $-2n$ and $n$, which are not covered by the existing results of Gorelik and Serganova. As a consequence, we obtain supercharacter identities, including the conjecture of Adamovi\'c and Milas as a special case.

papers.title: Effective Gromov-Witten computations for GKM spaces and a semisimple application
papers.abstract:
We report a major update to our original software GKMtools and record multiple improvements in the computation of Gromov--Witten invariants of GKM spaces. This includes a refined divisor equation that reduces the complexity from exponential to linear in the number of marked points, three tricks to accelerate the computation of curve class relations in the GKM graph, and an implementation of Mihalcea's algorithm for homogeneous varieties using the equivariant quantum Chevalley formula.
  As an application, we prove that the small quantum cohomology of the type-$E$ generalized Grassmannians $E_7/P_2,E_7/P_4,E_7/P_5,E_8/P_6$ is generically semisimple. These are precisely the remaining exceptional Grassmannians for which generic semisimplicity of small quantum cohomology was still unknown.

papers.title: Elementary Moves on Ideal Webs, Local Monodromies on Hitchin Fibrations, and Tropical Mutations on $\mathrm{K_0}$ Groups
papers.abstract:
This paper builds on the work of Goncharov by studying the correspondence between topological spectral covers constructed from generic $A_{m-1}$-webs with rank $m\ge2$, Hitchin spectral curves over good Hitchin loci, and the Grothendieck groups $K_0(\mathcal{D}_{\Gamma})$ associated with the quivers with potential $(Q_{\Gamma},W_{\Gamma})$ assigned to corresponding bipartite $A_{m-1}$-graphs.
  We show that the automorphisms on the non-frozen quiver lattices $\Lambda_{\Gamma}^{\circ}$ induced by compositions of elementary moves on ideal webs/bipartite graphs are the same as the Gauss--Manin monodromy actions on the $SL_m$ Hitchin fiber lattices $H_1(\operatorname{Prym}(\Sigma);\mathbb{Z})$ locally around discriminant loci. And the Gauss--Manin monodromy actions agree with the automorphisms on the Grothendieck groups $K_0(\mathcal{D}_{\Gamma}^{\circ})$ induced by compositions of mutations on the quivers with potential $(Q_{\Gamma},W_{\Gamma})$.

papers.title: Equivariant formality and representation theory
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a compact connected Lie group and $K$ its connected Lie subgroup. Using the $K$-theoretic version of equivariant formality developed in [F2] which involves analysis of vector bundles over $G/K$, we find two characterizations of equivariant formality of the isotropy action of $K$ on $G/K$. The first one equates equivariant formality with a "smoothness" condition of the restriction map of the representation ring of $G$ to that of $K$. The second characterization asserts that equivariant formality amounts to the equivariant $K$-theoretic index pairing of two certain special $K$-theory classes being nontrivial in some sense. By applying these characterizations, we are able to give a representation theoretic criterion for equivariant formality of the isotropy action by a circle subgroup, as well as an invariant theory criterion for the case where $K$ is a torus of dimension one less than the rank of $G$, culminating in a complete classification of equivariant formality where $G$ is further assumed to be simple.

papers.title: Finite group actions on the non-minimal nilpotent orbit closures in type A
papers.abstract: We study quotients of the closures of the nilpotent orbits of type A by finite groups of inner automorphisms. Assuming the nilpotent orbit is not minimal, we show that the Q-factorial terminalizations of quotients of nilpotent orbit closures are precisely the quotients of the symplectic resolutions of the orbit closures. This identifies the Mori fan of each Q-factorial terminalization of the quotient with the Mori fan of a symplectic resolution of the orbit closure.

papers.title: Finite Symplectic Automorphisms of Hyperk\"ahler Manifolds of $K3^{[n]}$-Type Act Trivially on Discriminant Groups
papers.abstract: We give an alternative proof of Mongardi's result that every finite group of symplectic automorphisms of a hyperk\"ahler manifold of $K3^{[n]}$-type acts trivially on the discriminant groups of its second cohomology lattice and its coinvariant lattice. The proof combines sphere-packing bounds, Vinberg's reflection chambers and structure results on even $2$-elementary lattices.

papers.title: Finite Tensor 2-Categories
papers.abstract:
We propose a definition of a finite linear 2-category, as a 2-categorical analogue of the notion of a finite abelian category of Etingof-Ostrik. We go on to prove that finite linear 2-categories with adjunctible projectives are precisely the Morita 2-categories of (all) algebras in a finite multitensor category. Thus, finite linear 2-categories with adjunctible projectives can be viewed as `non-semisimple' generalizations of the finite semisimple 2-categories of Douglas-Reutter.
  Secondly, we study finite multitensor 2-categories, that is, finite linear 2-categories equipped with a monoidal structure for which every objects has duals. We extend several results about fusion 2-categories to our present setting. In particular, we investigate the properties of the 2-category of bimodules over a rigid algebra $\mathcal{A}$ in a finite tensor 2-category $\mathfrak{C}$. We show that, if $\mathfrak{C}$ has adjunctible projectives, then the 2-category of $\mathcal{A}$-$\mathcal{A}$-bimodules in $\mathfrak{C}$ is a finite multitensor 2-category. This construction provides many examples of finite tensor 2-categories. For instance, the Drinfeld center of a finite tensor 2-category with adjunctible projectives is a finite tensor 2-category.

papers.title: From amplituhedra to flagtopes
papers.abstract: The amplituhedron was introduced by Arkani-Hamed and Trnka (2014) to geometrically encode scattering amplitudes in high-energy physics. It can be viewed as the generalization of a cyclic polytope into the Grassmannian, and is defined to be the projection of the totally nonnegative part of one Grassmannian with respect to a totally negative element of a second Grassmannian. We construct a Lie-theoretic generalization of amplituhedra called 'flag amplituhedra', by replacing the pair of Grassmannians in the definition with an arbitrary pair of partial flag varieties for a reductive group $G$. We study in detail an example of a flag amplituhedron which is not a Grassmannian amplituhedron; it is a curved hexagon in $\mathbb{P}^1\times \mathbb{P}^1$.

papers.title: Fukaya categories of surfaces with DG coefficients
papers.abstract:
Given a compact surface $S$ admitting a Liouville form, a finite set $Q \subset S$, a line field on $S$, and a local system of dg-categories on $S \setminus Q$ together with a section of the monodromy functor around each interior $q \in Q$, we construct a Fukaya category. We give examples where such Fukaya categories are quasi-equivalent to derived categories of projective completions of line bundles and of iterated blow-ups of the affine plane; and to wrapped Fukaya categories of cotangent bundles of spheres.
  We define two versions of the Fukaya category, a topological, which is constructed combinatorially from a full arc system, and a geometric, which includes all Lagrangian branes supported on immersed curves. We prove that the topological category embeds into the geometric category in an essentially unique way. To define Lagrangian branes we develop a generalisation of the Chekanov--Eliashberg algebra incorporating dg-coefficients and wrapping along the boundary.

papers.title: General position on Brauer--Severi surfaces
papers.abstract: The blowing-up of the projective plane at a finite set of points yields a del Pezzo surface if and only if the points lie in general position. In this note, we generalize this result to Brauer--Severi surfaces over arbitrary ground fields. Using Galois descent, intersection theory and combinatorial arguments, we provide explicit arithmetic and geometric conditions on the centre of the blowing-up.

papers.title: Geometric construction of Kashiwara crystals on multiparameter persistence
papers.abstract: We establish a geometric construction of Kashiwara crystals on the irreducible components of the varieties of multiparameter persistence modules. Our approach differs from the seminal work of Kashiwara and Saito, as well as subsequent related works, by emphasizing commutative relations rather than preprojective relations for a given quiver. Furthermore, we provide explicit descriptions of the Kashiwara operators in the fundamental cases of 1- and 2-parameter persistence modules, offering concrete insights into the crystal structure in these settings.

papers.title: Geometric priors for single-patch neural Calabi--Yau metrics on the quintic: a conservative fixed-$\psi$ Ablation study
papers.abstract: We investigate how geometric priors shape neural approximations of the complex Monge--Amp`ere equation on the quintic Calabi--Yau threefold. This fixed-$\psi$ diagnostic compares four single-patch ans"atze: a coordinate SIREN potential model, a direct-metric Cholesky baseline, an algebraic section ansatz, and a section-plus-neural hybrid. In a 96-run learning-rate and frequency archive, section-based models reach validation $\sigma=4.14$--$4.16%$, whereas SIREN and Cholesky remain at $41.29%$ and $44.27%$. Multi-seed controls use a shared affine-$\eta$ evaluator and five fresh validation clouds. Stable section settings give $3.84$--$4.77%$, compared with $28.46$--$30.59%$ for Cholesky and $34.73$--$38.13%$ for SIREN. Hybrid projective features do not improve best-case accuracy, but they stabilise the stressed regime. They limit $\sigma$ to $4.26$--$4.41%$, versus $4.45$--$205.45%$ for raw coordinates. Within this protocol, section-based geometric structure is the main driver of accuracy; coordinate-only models plateau at substantially higher error, and raw hybrid flexibility can amplify instability. We provide a projective-scaling derivation, document protocol asymmetries, and identify projectively consistent hybrid corrections as the next step.

papers.title: Gross--Prasad conjecture in geometric Langlands
papers.abstract: We prove part of the global Gross--Prasad conjecture for $G = \mathrm{SO}_{n} \times \mathrm{SO}_{n-1}$ and $H = \mathrm{SO}_{n-1}$ in the unramified de Rham geometric Langlands setting proposed by Ben-Zvi--Sakellaridis--Venkatesh.

papers.title: Hankel determinants and the length of finite Pierce expansions
papers.abstract: For integers $a>b>0$, let $P(a,b)$ be the number of steps the iteration $x\mapsto a \bmod x$ takes to reach $0$ from $b$; it is the length of the Pierce expansion of $b/a$. We prove $P(a,b)\ll_\varepsilon a^{\beta_*+\varepsilon}$, where $\beta_*=(41301-3\sqrt{82849})/137480=0.2941336553\ldots$, improving the exponent $1/3-2/177$ of Chase and Pandey. The tail of an orbit carries a sequence of positive integers, the Hankel determinants of a natural moment sequence, and these are small where the drops of the orbit are small. Grouping orbit states by such integers places the quotient differences of each group on curves of bounded degree, whose integer points we count with the uniform bounds of Castryck, Cluckers, Dittmann and Nguyen. The resulting exponent approaches $5/17$ when these curves have large degree relative to the logarithmic size of the box. We raise the degree by adjoining further integer invariants, by an effective Hilbert irreducibility sieve, and by an exact identity for the direction of the curvature vector, and come within $1.61\cdot10^{-5}$ of $5/17$. We also give an elementary proof of the exponent $3/10+\varepsilon$ and a bound for orbits whose quotient increments rarely rise. All results are formalised in Lean 4 with Mathlib. Shallit's conjectured $O((\log a)^2)$ bound remains open.

papers.title: Helly theorems for lattice of flats of a matroid
papers.abstract: A basis of a matroid is adapted to a flat if it contains a basis of the flat. We prove that a family of flats in a rank r matroid has a common adapted basis whenever every subfamily of at most r+1 flats does. The ground set and the family may be infinite; only the rank must be finite. This result, in particular, contains Klyachko's vector space Helly theorem for subspaces. As an application, we obtain a splitting criterion for tropical toric vector bundles on projective spaces. As a secondary application, we derive quadratic bounds for the Helly number for distributive generation in the lattice of flats.

papers.title: Highest weight vectors in queer Howe duality
papers.abstract: We use Gauss decomposition to study the singular vectors in the regular representation on the coordinate superalgebra of the big cell of the queer supergroup. This gives explicit bases for the highest weight spaces in queer Howe duality. As an application, the same method recovers the explicit highest weight vectors in the general linear case obtained by Cheng and Wang.

papers.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for nef bundles
papers.abstract: We introduce the $(m,p,q)$-Lefschetz property for $(1,1)$-type endomorphisms of Hodge--Lefschetz modules, providing a framework for studying nef $(1,1)$-classes and characteristic classes of nef vector bundles on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Under a Hall--Rado type condition on nef twisted vector bundles, we prove Hodge--Riemann relations for products of top Chern classes and, in suitable bidegrees, for products of derived Schur classes. For products of nef $(1,1)$-classes, we show furthermore that the Hall--Rado type condition is equivalent to simultaneous Hodge--Riemann relations. Our proofs build on the purity theorem and descent lemma of Cattani, Kaplan, and Schmid. We extend the descent lemma to Schur classes of nef vector bundles. We also establish formal analogs for projective bundle modules over Hodge--Lefschetz modules, with applications to tautological classes and descent on matroid Chow rings.

papers.title: Hypergeometric Motives from Toric Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study two compactifications of general hypersurfaces defined by the vanishing of linear combinations of $d+2$ monomials in $d$-dimensional algebraic tori. We prove that the number of their $\mathbb{F}_q$-points is given by finite hypergeometric sums under certain general conditions. In the process, we introduce the notion of a gamma triple, which allows us to extend the classical definition of finite hypergeometric sums to prime powers corresponding to the cyclotomic field of definition of the associated monodromy representation. As a special case of our main results, we study the Dwork family and obtain a formula for the number of its $\mathbb{F}_q$-points. Our results generalise the work of Beukers, Cohen, and Mellit for finite hypergeometric sums defined over $\mathbb{Q}$.

papers.title: Infinitely many elliptic curves with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$ and rank at least six
papers.abstract: We show that there are infinitely many elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with torsion subgroup $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$ and rank at least $6$, answering the case $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$ of Problem 2.6 in Dujella's list of open problems. The largest rank previously known to occur infinitely often with this torsion was $5$, due to Eroshkin. The curves are fibers of a one-parameter family of Dujella and Peral, which we show has rank exactly $3$ over the rational function field. The family is a base change of an elliptic K3 surface, and quadratic twists of that surface give it three further independent points over the function field of an elliptic curve of rank one. Congruences then carry the independence of the six points, and the torsion $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$, from one rational point of that curve to infinitely many. The result is unconditional. It contradicts the prediction of Park, Poonen, Voight and Wood that only finitely many curves with this torsion have rank greater than $5$, although the curves form a sparse family. A second family, over an elliptic curve of rank two, gives another proof.

papers.title: Integer points for iterated Weierstrass elliptic functions
papers.abstract: Iterated Weierstrass P functions exhibit relationships between period lattices and the dynamics. We connect the dynamical properties to the occurrence of integer and rational points on associated real elliptic curves. Defining a complex number z to be an integer point if both P(z) and P'(z) are integers, we restrict to P when the lattice is real and its invariants g2 and g3 are integers. We study when an integer point lies in the Fatou set of P and when it lies in the Julia set, and if there is any dynamical significance to this. Applying established results on integer solutions to cubic Diophantine equations to the dynamical properties of iterated elliptic P functions, we show integer points at poles of P lie in the Julia set. Integer points can also occur in the Fatou set of P.

papers.title: Integral Forms of Twisted Quantum Affine Algebras and Quantum Frobenius
papers.abstract: For twisted quantum affine algebras, we compare Lusztig's restricted integral form with the integral form generated by group-like toral elements and divided powers of real Drinfeld current modes. The two forms coincide over $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]$ outside type $A_{2n}^{(2)}$. In type $A_{2n}^{(2)}$, the smallest ordinary localization over which they coincide is $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}][\Phi_{4r}(q)^{-1}\mid r\geq1]$ when $n=1$, and $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}][\Phi_{8r}(q)^{-1}\mid r\geq1]$ when $n\geq2$, where $\Phi_k(q)$ are cyclotomic polynomials. In particular, no localization obtained by inverting finitely many nonzero Laurent polynomials suffices in this family.

papers.title: Iwahori Whittaker functions for unramified quasi-split groups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{G}$ be a connected unramified quasi-split reductive group defined over a nonarchimedean local field $F$. This paper concerns the Iwahori Whittaker functions attached to the unramified principal series of $\mathbf{G}(F)$. We introduce Demazure-Whittaker operators and show that in the non-split case they generate a Hecke algebra with unequal parameters that are determined by $\mathbf{G}$. We then connect these operators to the Whittaker functions, establishing formulas for calculating all values for a basis of Iwahori Whittaker functions and giving a new proof of the Casselman-Shalika formula for the spherical Whittaker function. In doing so we build on the work for split groups of Brubaker, Bump and Licata; the new feature here is the appearance of a Hecke algebra with unequal parameters.

papers.title: K3 surfaces with finite automorphism group in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: We classify K3 surfaces with finite automorphism group in positive characteristic. The classification is the same as over the complex numbers, except when the base field is $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$.

papers.title: Klt varieties with semipositive anticanonical bundle : symmetric tensors, holonomy and structure
papers.abstract: The aim of this article is to study klt projective varieties such that the anticanonical bundle is semipositive from the differential-geometric point of view. The study of the holonomy of such varieties yields generalizations of several results. We show that the dimension of the space of symmetric differentials is bounded by a constant depending on the augmented irregularity, generalizing a result of Kobayashi. If we endow such a variety $X$ with a metric $\omega$ whose Ricci curvature is non-negative, then we show that the holonomy of the regular locus is compact. If we assume that $X$ has canonical singularities, then we show that the general fiber of the Albanese map can be decomposed into a product of irreducible Calabi-Yau varieties, irreducible holomorphic symplectic varieties and hereditarily rationally connected varieties by the holonomy generalizing a structure theorem of Campana, Demailly and Peternell. To conclude, we show that the fundamental group of the regular locus of such varieties is virtually abelian.

papers.title: Lefschetz coefficients of quantum theta functions
papers.abstract: We prove that the coefficients of quantum theta functions in the skew-symmetric setting are characters of finite-dimensional \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) representations. This proves Conjectures 1.4, 2.17 and 3.13 of Davison–Mandel and the two-wall conjecture stated as Conjecture 3.12 in Davison’s ICM 2026 survey.

papers.title: Les Houches lecture notes on topological recursion
papers.abstract: You may have seen the words "topological recursion" mentioned in papers on matrix models, Hurwitz theory, Gromov-Witten theory, topological string theory, knot theory, topological field theory, JT gravity, cohomological field theory, free probability theory, gauge theories, to name a few. The goal of these lecture notes is certainly not to explain all these applications of the topological recursion framework. Rather, the intention is to provide a down-to-earth (and hopefully accessible) introduction to topological recursion itself, so that when you see these words mentioned, you can understand what it is all about. These lecture notes accompanied a series of lectures at the Les Houches school "Quantum Geometry (Mathematical Methods for Gravity, Gauge Theories and Non-Perturbative Physics)" in Summer 2024.

papers.title: Limit Computation Over Posets via Minimal Initial Functors
papers.abstract: It is well known that limits can be computed by restricting along an initial functor, and that this often simplifies limit computation. We systematically study the algorithmic implications of this idea for diagrams indexed by a poset. We say an initial functor $F\colon C\to D$ with $C$ small is minimal if the sets of objects and morphisms of $C$ each have minimum cardinality, among the sources of all initial functors with target $D$. For $Q$ a finite poset or $Q\subseteq \mathbb N^d$ an interval (i.e., a convex, connected subposet), we describe all minimal initial functors $F\colon P\to Q$. In particular, we show that such $F$ is always a subposet inclusion, up to isomorphism. We give efficient algorithms to compute a choice of minimal initial functor. In the case that $Q\subseteq \mathbb N^d$ is an interval, we give asymptotically optimal bounds on $|\hom P|$, the number of relations in $P$ (including identities), in terms of the number $n$ of minima of $Q$: We show that $|\hom P|=\Theta(n)$ for $d\leq 3$, and $|\hom P|=\Theta(n^2)$ for $d>3$. We apply these results to give new bounds on the cost of computing $\lim G$ for a functor $G \colon Q\to \mathbf{Vec}$ valued in vector spaces. For $Q$ connected, we also give new bounds on the cost of computing the generalized rank of $G$ (i.e., the rank of the induced map $\lim G\to \operatorname{colim} G$), which is of interest in topological data analysis.

papers.title: Localization of weighted Goldman volume on $\mathrm{SL}(3,\R)$-Hitchin Component
papers.abstract: We compute Goldman volume on the moduli space of convex real projective structures on a closed oriented surface of genus at least two, with exponential weight defined by the shifted Blaschke area. For every positive parameter, the integral converges and is a finite sum of inverse powers of that parameter. Its coefficients are intersection numbers involving the bundle of regular cubic differentials on the moduli stack of stable curves. The proof establishes absolute convergence and vanishing signed boundary integrals of the transgression under simultaneous plumbing degeneration. The pushforward of Goldman measure by the shifted Blaschke area therefore has a polynomial density on $[0,\infty)$, and its sublevel volumes are polynomial in the threshold.

papers.title: Maximal geometric quotients of flag varieties
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of maximal geometric quotient, namely a geometric quotient of a polarized pair under a torus action which has a birational contraction to any other GIT quotient. For the action of the maximal torus on a complete flag variety, we show that a maximal geometric quotient exists and it is a Mori dream space, and its Cox ring is isomorphic to the Cox ring of the flag variety. We discuss birational properties of the maximal geometric quotients, their relations with the Chow quotients and explain how to construct them for maximal torus actions on flag varieties.

papers.title: Minimal depth $K$-types for wild double covers and Shimura correspondences
papers.abstract:
Using distinguished pseudo-spherical representations of covering tori constructed in a companion work and Dat's parahoric induction, we construct a distinguished family of representations for an Iwahori subgroup $\bar{I}$ in $\bar{G}$, an $n$-fold Brylinski-Deligne (BD) cover of a split connected reductive $p$-adic group $G$, under explicit hypotheses on the BD datum. No tameness assumption $\mathrm{gcd}(p,n)=1$ is imposed.
  The construction suggests a conjectural theory of Iwahori-types for BD covers beyond the tame case. We verify this for $2$-fold covers of almost simple simply-laced simply-connected Chevalley groups of rank at least $2$ over $2$-adic fields. In particular, for these non-tame $2$-fold covers we prove:
  1) The pair $(\bar{I},\sigma)$ is a Bushnell-Kutzko type for the Bernstein block analogous to the block of unramified principal series in a linear reductive group. This is a non-tame analogue of the Borel-Casselman theorem.
  2) The Hecke algebra $\mathcal{H}(\bar{G},\bar{I},\sigma^{\vee})$ has an Iwahori-Matsumoto presentation up to normalization. In types $A_{r},D_{2r+1},E_{6},E_{7}$ we obtain the complete presentation and show that $\mathcal{H}(\bar{G},\bar{I},\sigma^{\vee})$ is isomorphic to the Iwahori-Hecke algebra of an explicit linear group. This determines an equivalence of Bernstein blocks producing a local Shimura correspondence.
  3) The representation $\sigma$ extends to a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup $\bar{K}$. Among the genuine $\bar{K}$-representations, $\sigma$ has minimal depth with respect to the principal congruence filtration. It also yields a finite Shimura correspondence, generalizing a result of Savin.

papers.title: Mirror functor for deformed preprojective algebras
papers.abstract:
We construct noncommutative mirrors from the bulk-deformed Floer theory of compact immersed Lagrangians equipped with higher rank flat bundles, whose Floer theory can have non-zero curvature terms due to contributions of stable constant discs. For a nodal union of Lagrangian spheres, codimension-two bulk cycles meeting the compact core produce the additive deformed preprojective relations and the corresponding framed Maurer-Cartan spaces at nonzero complex moment-map levels. In particular, our localized mirror functors produce noncommutative ADHM and Nakajima monadic complexes. We obtain local charts and gluing maps of the noncommutative mirror varieties via explicit computations of Lagrangian deformation spaces and Fukaya isomorphisms between them. These constructions recover noncommutative spaces studied by Kapustin-Kuznetsov-Orlov, Baranovsky-Ginzburg-Kuznetsov, and Kawamata, with further examples in dimension three.
  We also establish the categorical framework in the unobstructed setting. For a compact $\mathbb Z$-graded unobstructed immersed Lagrangian $\mathbb{L}$ without nonpositive-degree immersed generators, Koszul duality identifies the derived Fukaya subcategory generated by $\mathbb{L}$ with the derived category of modules with finite-dimensional total cohomology over its extended localized mirror $\tilde{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{L}}$. This construction starts from the Floer algebra of the compact reference brane and does not require a global wrapped generator. Applications to plumbings recover known split-generation results for compact objects.

papers.title: Multiplicity One for Unitary Ginzburg--Rallis Models over Local Fields
papers.abstract: We prove multiplicity at most one for the unitary similitude Ginzburg--Rallis model over local fields of characteristic zero, for both the quasi-split and non-quasi-split groups. The theorem holds for all irreducible smooth representations over non-Archimedean fields and all irreducible Casselman--Wallach representations over the real field. We first describe the decomposition into parabolic double cosets and compute the required stabilizers. Over a non-Archimedean field we use character obstructions, localization, and transpose symmetry. Over the real field we use a Casimir identity and explicit normal vectors to prove the corresponding statement for distributions with prescribed infinitesimal character. The Gelfand--Kazhdan criterion and a dualizing involution then give the multiplicity bound.

papers.title: Mutation-acyclicity in rank four is decidable but not semialgebraic
papers.abstract: We prove that mutation-acyclicity of quivers on four vertices is decidable. If a four-vertex quiver $Q$ is mutation-acyclic, then some sequence of mutations takes it to an acyclic quiver without any arrow multiplicity exceeding $\operatorname{max}\{\operatorname{ht}(Q),m(Q)\}$, where $\operatorname{ht}(Q)$ is the largest arrow multiplicity of $Q$ and $m(Q)$ is the Markov invariant of Fomin and Neville evaluated on the totally proper wiggle class of $Q$. A search within a computable form of this bound decides mutation-acyclicity of four-vertex quivers with $O(h^{24})$ states for input height $h\ge1$. Together with a theorem of Caldero and Keller, it also decides mutation equivalence of two four-vertex quivers up to relabeling whenever one of them is mutation-acyclic. We conjecture that $\operatorname{ht}(Q)$ alone suffices as the bound, which would reduce the search to $O(h^{6})$ states, and we verify this for all four-vertex quivers of height at most three. In the other direction, for every $n\ge4$ we construct an affine family of connected $n$-vertex quivers whose nonnegative even members are mutation-acyclic and whose positive odd members are mutation-cyclic. Consequently, unlike in rank three, no fixed finite Boolean combination of polynomial equations and strict polynomial inequalities in the arrow weights (i.e., a semialgebraic criterion) decides mutation-acyclicity of $n$-vertex quivers, even allowing polynomials that are not mutation-invariant. Finally, we correct the criterion for four-vertex quivers of height at most two stated in our earlier paper, and recover its classification counts with short certificates. The calculations in the proof of the height bound are verified by computer for all values of their parameters.

papers.title: Non-split groups of Lie type and iSchur algebras with unequal parameters
papers.abstract: We present a geometric framework for realizing quantum Schur algebras with unequal parameters, via constructible sheaves on flag varieties arising from non-split groups of Lie type. In the special cases of general unitary groups and minus-type orthogonal groups, this framework yields the iSchur algebras with unequal parameters, which are closely related to the quasi-split iquantum groups of type AIII. Such a geometric realization enables the construction of canonical bases, integral forms, and monoidal categorification for these unequal-parameter iSchur algebras and the corresponding iquantum groups. This material is not a formal generalization from the equal-parameter case to the unequal-parameter case. A nontrivial arithmetic structure is imposed on the geometric structure of split groups, giving rise to many new phenomena. For example, the support varieties of generators of an integral form may not be rationally smooth, the categorification is provided by the category of descent data of semisimple complexes fixed by the twisted Frobenius, and the positivity of the canonical basis is established using a refined covering.

papers.title: Nonvanishing implies abundance
papers.abstract: We prove that the nonvanishing conjecture implies the abundance conjecture.

papers.title: On $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundles on $\mathbb{P}^3$ that are small modifications of a Fano fourfold
papers.abstract: We find necessary conditions for the projectivization of a rank two vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ on $\mathbb{P}^3_{\mathbb{C}}$ to be related to a smooth Fano 4-fold by a small $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial modification (SQM). Furthermore, we fully describe the birational geometry of $\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{P}^3}(\mathcal{E})$ when $\mathcal{E}$ is stable, with $c_1=-1$, $c_2=2$. In this case, we prove that there exists a flip from $X^+$ to $\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{P}^3}(\mathcal{E})$, where $X^+$ is smooth and Fano. We also determine the birational geometry and numerical invariants of $X^+$.

papers.title: On counting satisfying assignments via polynomial separation
papers.abstract: We give a preliminary exposition of a qualitative form of the main result of OpenAI's preprint "The Exponential Time Hypothesis is false": for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, $3$-SAT on $n$ variables with $m$ clauses can be decided in time $O_\varepsilon(2^{\varepsilon n}(n+m)^{O(1)})$ and polynomial space. We separate the general counting procedure from the construction that supplies its input. The procedure deforms the clause inputs so that, at designated points, the count factors into local sums, from which Hermite interpolation recovers the original count; the construction builds such deformations from coordinate swaps in a tensor basis, leveraging a parity interpolation in the spirit of Alman and Williams.

papers.title: On finite covers of projective spaces, generic outside of codimension three
papers.abstract: In the article, we generalize to an arbitrary dimension results obtained by the author and S.Yu. Nemirovski that related to Chisini's conjecture claimed that if $B$ is the discriminant of two generic covers $f_i:X_i\to \mathbb P^2$, $i=1,2$, and $\max (\deg f_1,\deg f_2) \geq 5$, then $f_1$ and $f_2$ are equivalent covers.

papers.title: On Open Borel Orbits in Conormal Bundles to Schubert Cells
papers.abstract: Let $C(v)$ denote a Schubert cell in the flag variety $\operatorname{GL}_n/B$, and let $X(w)$ be a Schubert variety containing $C(v)$. Mellit has conjectured that, if $X(w)$ is smooth, the existence of an open $B$-orbit in the conormal bundle to $C(v)$ in $X(w)$ is equivalent to $C(w_0w)$ being contained in the smooth locus of $X(w_0v)$. We prove a stronger version of this conjecture, requiring only that $X(w)$ is factorial. We prove our result by constructing a sequence of graphs associated to the pair $v,w$ such that the existence of a cycle in one of these graphs is equivalent to the non-existence of such an open orbit.

papers.title: On some positivity properties of the Riemann $\Xi$ function
papers.abstract: We prove strict log-concavity of the positive functions $\Theta$ and $\Lambda$ with one-sided and bilateral Laplace transforms $1/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)$ and $1/\Xi$, respectively, where $\Xi(z)=\xi(\tfrac12+iz)$. For either function, log-concavity is the Pólya frequency property of order two (PF$_2$). Without assuming RH, but using known zero verification through height $3\cdot10^{12}$, we further prove that $\Lambda$ is a PF function of order ten (PF$_{10}$). We also prove local PF positivity for $\Theta$: for each fixed order, the ordered minors of $\Theta(x-y)$ are positive when all differences $x_i-y_j$ are sufficiently small and positive. Additionally, we prove the generalized Laguerre inequalities: if RH holds up to height $T>1/2$, then $L_n[\Xi](x)\ge0$ for every $n\ge0$ and $|x|\le T-1/2$; the case $n=1$ is due to Csordas, Ruttan and Varga (1991).

papers.title: On the $d$-invariants of Brieskorn spheres and $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$
papers.abstract: We study the $d$-invariant from Heegaard Floer homology for Brieskorn spheres $\Sigma(p,q,r)$. Using surgeries on two singular fibers, we establish new relations of the $d$-invariants among various Brieskorn spheres. For $p=2$, we show that $d$ never vanishes if $q/r$ lies in certain intervals on the rational line. Altogether, we completely classify Brieskorn spheres $\Sigma(2,q,r)$ with $d=0$. The zero set is expressed using submonoids of $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ and the Stern--Brocot tree. As an application, we prove that most Brieskorn spheres $\Sigma(2,q,r)$ do not bound a rational homology $4$-ball.

papers.title: On the existence of polarized varieties without weakly Ulrich bundles
papers.abstract: We give an obstruction to the existence of bundles $\mathcal E$ on a smooth $n$-dimensional polarized variety such that $\mathcal E$ is $a$-regular and ${\mathcal E}^*(K_X+(n+1)H)$ is $b$-regular. In particular, this gives an obstruction to the existence of weakly Ulrich bundles. Using the latter and some recent examples of [A1] in dimension $2$, we prove that for any $n \ge 2$ there exist many smooth $n$-dimensional varieties $X$ with a very ample line bundle $H$, such that there is no weakly Ulrich bundle for $(X,H)$.

papers.title: On the rank of the double cohomology of moment-angle complexes
papers.abstract: In [6], the authors construct a cochain complex $C\!H^*(\mathcal{Z}_{\mathcal{K}})$ on the cohomology of a moment-angle complex $\mathcal{Z}_{\mathcal{K}}$ and call the resulting cohomology the double cohomology, $H\!H^*(\mathcal{Z}_{\mathcal{K}})$. In this paper, we study the change of rank in double cohomology after gluing an $n$-simplex to a simplicial complex $\mathcal{K}$ in certain conditions. As an application, we give a positive answer to an open problem in [6]: For any even integer $r$, there always exists a simlicial complex $\mathcal{K}$ such that $\operatorname{rank} H\!H^*(\mathcal{Z}_{\mathcal{K}})=r$.

papers.title: On Thom Polynomials for $\mathcal{A}$-singularities of parametric curves and degeneracy loci formulas
papers.abstract: In this research article, we make an in-depth investigation of the computations for Thom Polynomials for $\mathcal{A}$-singularities of parametric curves germs in the plane and space cases using the framework established by Ohmoto and the Restriction Method introduced by Rim\'anyi, and we also propose a geometric way for such computations using degeneracy loci Chern classes formulas proven by Fulton, which seems a promising way to generalize the Thom Polynomial expression for the stabilization of such singularities in $\mathbb{C}^N$, depending exclusively on $N$ as a parameter.

papers.title: Parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^n$ and its Complete Resolution
papers.abstract: We formulate a parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^{n}$ by incorporating independent scale parameters into the linear part of a polynomial map via polar decomposition. We prove that requiring the Jacobian determinant to remain constant uniformly across the parameter space decouples the Jacobian equation into a system enforcing the vanishing of all principal minors of the perturbation matrix. This system strictly forces lower triangularization up to variable permutations, establishing a necessary and sufficient condition for polynomial invertibility and providing an explicit, canonical scheme for constructing the inverse map in every dimension.

papers.title: Periodic Forcing, Echo Constraints and the Non-Periodicity of the Rule 30 Centre Column: Reductions, Structural Lemmas, Certified Computations and Barriers
papers.abstract: Wolfram's Rule 30 Prize Problem 1 asks whether the centre column of Rule 30, started from a single lit cell, is ever eventually periodic. We study the problem through a half-line system driven by a periodic boundary signal. Combining a known local identity with the standard reduction to finite seeds, Problem 1 follows from a single statement, the Echo Lemma: no finite half-line configuration driven by a non-constant periodic boundary can satisfy, at every lit boundary minute, the identity that Rule 30 forces on the neighbour of the centre. Around this formulation we prove a collection of exact structural results: a dependence-window lemma and a merging criterion for reconstructed columns, triangularity and monotonicity of the finite-support constraints, a forced-creation identity at boundary bounces, a description of the infinite survivors as a full shift for period two, and, for the two-sided period-two problem, uniqueness of the compatible left half together with exact forced identities near the centre, including a half-column that must vanish identically. For the linear relative Rule 150 we prove the analogue of the Echo Lemma for every odd period by a Frobenius self-similarity argument, and we identify exactly the two steps that fail for Rule 30. We report exhaustive and SAT-certified computations excluding counterexamples of bounded width, and we document a set of barriers: every exact mechanism found is confined to a bounded neighbourhood of the centre, no additive conserved quantity of small range exists, and the sideways reconstruction has a growing number of distinguishable states. The Echo Lemma, and with it Problem 1, remains open; the contribution of this article is a verified framework, labelled throughout as proved, certified or open.

papers.title: Pointwise to global good reduction problems
papers.abstract: Given a smooth proper family of varieties over some $p$-adic field, if (sufficiently many of) the closed fibers have good reduction, does the family as a whole have good reduction? This question is asked and positively answered in recent work of Cadoret-Tamagawa for curves in general, and abelian varieties if the base field has absolute ramification at most $p-1$. In this paper we define a general framework for studying this question, yielding new positive answers for families of K3 surfaces and cubic fourfoulds, again with ramification at most $p-1$. Our strategy is to study several extension properties of moduli spaces and how they transfer under various morphisms. Of particular importance are integral canonical models of Shimura varieties, and whether or not their extension properties are preserved under ramified scalar extension. Additionally, building on earlier counterexamples by Raynaud-Ogus-Gabber and Vasiu-Zink, we show that the ramification assumption is optimal for the result of Cadoret-Tamagawa on families of abelian varieties. This reflects the fact that the extension property of Siegel Shimura varieties no longer holds over a field of absolute ramification at least $p$.

papers.title: Quartic Keller Maps and Tameness in Three Variables
papers.abstract: We study invertibility and tameness for polynomial maps of affine three-space of total degree at most four. We prove that every complex Keller map in this degree range is a polynomial automorphism and, independently, that every complex polynomial automorphism of total degree at most four is tame. The invertibility argument combines homogeneous factorization of the leading part, invariant rings of conic pencils, and residue obstructions on cubic fibers. The tameness argument uses a criterion based on a constant second directional derivative, low-degree coordinate classifications, and local tameness of plane polynomial automorphisms over a polynomial parameter ring. The invertibility conclusion extends to every field of characteristic zero.

papers.title: Rank reduction in orthosymplectic types
papers.abstract: This note establishes a rank reduction for RLL-realization of quantum affine supergroups of orthosymplectic type. In the rational limit, this provides a more conceptual proof of the analogous result for orthosymplectic superYangians from arXiv:2311.18818. We also determine the exact scalar prefactor appearing in the evaluation of the universal $R$-matrix, refining the main result of arXiv:2408.16720.

papers.title: Rank two cohomology jump loci on projective varieties
Re-framing the classification of ideals in noncommutative tensor triangular geometry
papers.abstract: We prove that a 'pseudo-Hochster dual' of the noncommutative Balmer spectrum of a monoidal triangulated category classifies its semiprime thick tensor ideals. This extends Balmer's classification of radical thick tensor ideals to noncommutative tensor triangular geometry. To achieve this, we utilize the notion of support data for lattices and frames, under which the classification follows via Stone duality. We also give a characterization for when the noncommutative Balmer spectrum behaves as it does in tensor triangular geometry, that is, when it is a spectral space with quasi-compact opens given by complements of supports. Finally, we show that rigid centrally generated monoidal triangulated categories satisfy this property, and we answer a question posed by Negron--Pevtsova regarding classification of one-sided tensor ideals via cohomological support.

papers.title: Relative derived delooping levels and torsion intervals
papers.abstract: Let $U$ be a support $\tau$-tilting module over a finite dimensional algebra $A$, and let $\mathcal{V}\subseteq \text{Fac}U$ be any torsion class. The heart $\mathcal H=\text{Fac} U\cap \mathcal{V}^\perp$ inherits the exact structure from mod$A$ and admits an Ext-progenerator $P$. Let $B=\text{End}_A(P)$. We define the relative derived delooping level on the exact heart $\mathcal H$ and compare it with the relative delooping level on $\mathcal {H}$ and the derived delooping level of $B$. We show that $\text{Findim} B^{op}$ is bounded by the relative derived delooping level on the $\mathcal H$. For a wide heart, the relative derived delooping level on the heart equals the derived delooping level of $B$. We obtain explicit bounds from representation-finite relative syzygy strata and characterize global first-order finiteness using an Ext-injective cogenerator.

papers.title: Representation and abelianization growth, particularly along expanding sequences
papers.abstract: We study two obstructions to a finite group $G$ having a generating $d$-tuple whose Cayley graph has spectral gap at least $\epsilon$. Lubotzky and Weiss proved that such a gap forces $\mathrm{ab}_k(G)$, the largest order of the abelianization of a subgroup of index at most $k$, to be $\exp(O_\epsilon(dk))$, while de la Harpe, Robertson and Valette proved that it forces $\mathrm{rep}_k(G)$, the number of irreducible complex representations of degree at most $k$, to be $\exp(O_\epsilon(dk^2))$. We show that the first bound implies the second, and in fact implies it with $k^2$ replaced by $k\log k$. For this, we prove that every finite $d$-generated group satisfies the inequality $\mathrm{rep}_k(G)\leq\exp((d-1)k\log k+O(dk))\cdot\mathrm{ab}_k(G)$, regardless of its spectral gap. The leading term $(d-1)k\log k$ is attained by powers of alternating groups, and it disappears for groups without large alternating sections. The proof reduces to counting the finite primitive subgroups of $\mathrm{GL}_m(\mathbf{C})$, and we show that there are at most $\exp(O(\log^4m))$ of them up to conjugacy and scalars. Wigderson asked whether $k^2$ in the second bound can be lowered to $k$, so our result answers his question up to a logarithm. We do not know whether the logarithm is actually needed. For powers of alternating groups, the natural candidates, we show that a spectral gap keeps the number of factors a fixed power below the maximum allowed by $d$-generation, and that random generators have spectral gap tending to $0$ already for superpolynomially many factors.

papers.title: Representations of shifted quantum affine algebras and cluster algebras II: Non simply-laced types and cluster expansions
papers.abstract: We extend our previous results on cluster structures in the Grothendieck rings of categories $\mathcal{O}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ for shifted quantum affine algebras to the non-simply laced types. We also show that, for all types, the formal power series expressions of the cluster monomials in terms of classes of positive prefundamental representations can be regarded as limits of cluster expansions, thus establishing their positivity.

papers.title: Semisimple module categories with fusion rules of the compact flag manifold type
papers.abstract: We classify semisimple left module categories over the representation category of a type A quantum group whose fusion rules arise from Levi subalgebras. The classification is connected to equivariant Poisson structures on compact flag manifolds in the operator-algebraic setting, and on semisimple coadjoint orbits in the algebraic setting. We also provide an explicit construction based on the BGG categories of deformed quantum enveloping algebras, whose unitarizability corresponds to being of quotient type. Finally, we present a brief discussion of the non-quantum group case

papers.title: Small degree isogenies between conjugate principally polarized superspecial abelian surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $p>3$ be a prime number. We prove that every principally polarized superspecial abelian surface over $\mathbb{F}_{p^{2}}$ with $p^{2}$-Frobenius $[-p]$ admits a separable polarized isogeny to its Frobenius conjugate with multiplier at most $(p^{3}/2)^{1/5}$. This generalizes a recent result of Aubry, Oyono, and Vincent (2026, arXiV:2607.14624) who proved that every supersingular elliptic curve defined over $\bar{\mathbb{F}}_{p}$ admits an isogeny to its Frobenius conjugate with degree at most $(p/2)^{1/3}$.

papers.title: Smooth quotients of principally polarized abelian varieties
papers.abstract: We give an explicit characterization of all principally polarized abelian varieties $(A,\Theta)$ such that there is a finite subgroup of automorphisms $G$ of $A$ that preserve the numerical class of $\Theta$, and such that the quotient variety $A/G$ is smooth. We also give a complete classification of smooth quotients of Jacobians of curves.

papers.title: Smoothing Calabi-Yau threefolds with nodes and del Pezzo cone points
papers.abstract: We give a necessary and sufficient homological criterion for smoothing projective Calabi-Yau threefolds with nodes and anticanonical cones over smooth del Pezzo surfaces of degrees five, six and seven, or over a smooth quadric surface. For some choice of local smoothing components, the criterion requires a relation on a crepant resolution among link classes whose associated local parameters avoid every discriminant. The complexified relation space describes first-order deformations modulo locally trivial ones. Necessity follows from local period and vanishing-cycle arguments; sufficiency applies Friedman's unobstructedness theorem to a crepant partial resolution. Whenever the criterion holds, the deformation space on the chosen components is smooth. A nonsmoothable example, whose deformation space is reduced with four smooth components, shows why nonvanishing at every singular point is insufficient. We also construct a smoothable Batyrev hypersurface admitting no smoothing induced by proper ambient families obtained from Minkowski decompositions at a single lattice degree.

papers.title: Some Coble surfaces admit only Bertini involutions
papers.abstract: In this article we show that a biregular involution $i : X \to X$ defined on an unnodal Coble surface $X$ with irreducible boundary curve $\{C\} = |- 2 K_X|$ is necessarily a lift of a Bertini involution. Then we show with counterexamples that the hypothesis of irreducibility of $C$ and unnodality of $X$ are both necessary.

papers.title: Some exposition of “The Exponential Time Hypothesis Is False”
