papers.abstract: This is an exposition of the paper "The Exponential Time Hypothesis Is False" by OpenAI [Oct. 26, 2026], produced through discussion with an LLM. Among other things, it tries to highlight the approximating polynomial for parity, and writes the matrix version of this polynomial using (a light amount of) quantum language.

papers.title: Some notes on tensor triangular geometry
papers.abstract:
These are notes from the lectures I gave at the Oberwolfach seminar `Tensor Triangular Geometry and Interactions' which was held in October 2025.
  The aim of these notes is to give an introduction to tensor triangular geometry, for both small and large categories, through the lens of lattice theory. We do not try to be exhaustive and this is reflected in both the content and the bibliography. For instance we are quite light on triangulated preliminaries, especially for compactly generated categories.
  The first three sections treat the essentially small case and conclude with a tensor triangular proof of Thomason's theorem computing the spectrum of the perfect complexes on a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. The last section treats the compactly generated case. This final section is somewhat experimental and contains some new thoughts.

papers.title: Stability conditions on products of curves and Hilbert schemes of surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that stability conditions on the derived category of a product of curves of positive genus are uniquely determined by their central charge and the phase of skyscraper sheaves. As an application, we construct stability conditions on Hilbert schemes of points on certain surfaces, including some K3 surfaces of Kummer type.

papers.title: Sun's supercongruence for an Apéry-like sequence
papers.abstract: Let $a_n=\sum_{j=0}^n\binom{n}{j}^2\binom{2j}{j}$. We prove that, for every prime $p>3$, the sum $(-1)^{(p-1)/2}\sum_{n=0}^{p-1}\binom{2n}{n}a_n/54^n$ is congruent modulo $p^2$ to $4x^2-2p$ when $p=x^2+3y^2\equiv1\pmod3$, and to zero when $p\equiv2\pmod3$. For the latter primes a quadratic differential invariant of the truncated generating polynomial lifts Sun's congruence modulo $p$. For the former primes we certify two modular periods directly by identities of weight eight, construct a Hecke polynomial with an explicit degree bound, and specialize a finite polynomial identity at a complex multiplication point. The coefficient at degree $p$ and both parity cases of the complex multiplication matrices are treated explicitly. A corresponding evaluation of the Franel sum with denominator $50$ follows by the same arguments.

papers.title: Tautological modular forms of level two and degree two
papers.abstract: We show how to use divisors on the projectivized Hodge bundle to construct special vector-valued modular forms and then apply invariant theory to construct all vector-valued Siegel modular forms of level two and degree two. Thus we construct all modular forms in terms of certain basic modular forms that are intimately connected to the moduli of curves of genus two.

papers.title: Thakur's Conjectures in Function Field Arithmetic: A Report On Queries to Frontier Agents
papers.abstract: This report was created on 23 October 2026 from six AI research reports generated with the frontier-dump skill on Dinesh Thakur's conjectures in function field arithmetic. Taylor Dupuy initiated those queries during his talk How to Use AI in Mathematical Research Effectively at the University of Rochester Number Theory Seminar on that date. The six reports were synthesized with harvest-dumps and developed into this manuscript with using-latexpowers. We survey the current status of several conjectures of Dinesh Thakur and his coauthors on the arithmetic of $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$: the degree hypotheses for power sums, the characterisation of zeta-like multizeta values in genus zero and in higher genus, the relations among multizeta values, the distribution of zeros of Goss zeta functions, and the automata-theoretic transcendence questions for special values. For each conjecture we give the precise statement and its status in the literature. The six computational research dumps report several results and refutations. Among them, the recursion predicted by Thakur's second power-sum hypothesis fails for an explicit family of exponents at thirteen non-prime values of $q$ (a computer-assisted result); the shuffle relations, even with Frobenius and Carlitz's Eulerian evaluations, do not generate all relations among multizeta values; a closed formula for a $v$-adic valuation difference conjectured by Thakur holds only after a sign change (and, for $d\ge4$, halving), and the corrected formula is proved, with computer assistance, for degrees $d\le 11$; and the $v$-adic Newton polygon of a Goss zeta function over $\mathbb{F}_2[t]$ at a prime of degree two has a slope of multiplicity one, which appears to contradict a result claimed in a 2023 preprint (this conflict needs human verification). The shuffle result and an assembly of published theorems describing all relations are elementary, and we claim no novelty for them. We also write out a proof of a theorem of Wen and Yao on $v$-adic arithmetic gamma values. Computational evidence is labelled as such throughout, and the open problems are listed. This manuscript is AI-generated by Claude Code (model claude-opus-5-5) from AI-generated research dumps; its proofs received only AI review, and no human has checked them.

papers.title: The double of a simplicial complex
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of doubling and r-tupling for simplicial complexes, a notion reminiscent to that of matching complexes in graph theory. We prove a connectivity result for such complexes and relate r-tupling to stabilizing r times faster in homological stability.

papers.title: The Generalized Vanishing Conjecture: The Two-Variable Theorem and the First Failing Dimension
The Lefschetz standard conjectures for 4d-dimensional Kummer-type hyper-Kaehler varieties
papers.abstract: We prove the Lefschetz standard conjectures for 4d-dimensional projective varieties of generalized Kummer deformation type. Along the way, we prove a generalization of a theorem of Buchweitz and Flenner in the analytic setting

papers.title: The Legendre potential and the gradient case of the differential Galois criterion for the Jacobian Conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $h\in\C[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ have constant nonzero Hessian determinant, let $h^{*}$ be its formal Legendre transform and $g=\vv{X,\grad h}-h$. The Nambu derivations of $\grad h$ satisfy $\delta_i(g)=X_i$ and $\delta^\alpha(g)=(\partial^\alpha h^{*})\circ\grad h$. Consequently, in the gradient case the differential Galois criterion of \cite{ACH19}, consisting of $n$ membership conditions, reduces to a single membership condition. Equivalently, $\grad h$ is a polynomial automorphism if and only if $g\in\C[\partial_1h,\dots,\partial_nh]$. Moreover, $\grad h$ is a polynomial automorphism if and only if $\delta^\alpha(g)=0$ for $|\alpha|=(\deg h-1)^{n-1}+2$, and then the coefficients $\delta^\alpha(g)(x_0)/\alpha!$ of $h^{*}$ at $\grad h(x_0)$ determine the inverse. If the Hessian determinant of $h$ is merely a nonzero polynomial, then $g$ is still a primitive element of $\C(X)$ over $\C(\partial_1h,\dots,\partial_nh)$. For the Nambu-tower criterion, doubling a Keller map yields no independent conditions. After an affine change of coordinates putting $\grad h$ in the normal form $X+H$, the formal Legendre transform is the sum of the formal Pascal difference series of $g$, and the termination of this series implies polynomial invertibility. In at most three variables the normal form of every gradient Keller map has strongly nilpotent Jacobian part and is therefore Pascal finite, by a theorem of de Bondt, and an explicit gradient automorphism in four variables has a normal form which is not Pascal finite. The five-variable counterexample of Meng and Yang shows that the properties used here do not imply the Hessian conjecture. The results do not settle the open cases $\JC_2$ and $\HC_4$.

papers.title: The numerical range of limits of real rational functions
papers.abstract: Given two nonzero polynomials $f, g \in \mathbb{R}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ vanishing at the origin $0 \in \mathbb{R}^n$, we study the numerical range of the limit $$ \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{f(x)}{g(x)}, $$ denoted by $\mathcal{R}_{f,g}$, which is defined as the set of all possible limits of the rational function $\displaystyle\frac{f}{g}$ as $x$ tends to $0$. When $n = 2$ and $g$ has a non-isolated zero at $0$, we describe all possible forms of $\mathcal{R}_{f,g}$ and provide an effective algorithm to compute this set based on Puiseux expansions. This is a follow-up to our recent results~\cite{Dinh2025}, in which we only considered the case when $0$ is an isolated zero of $g$.

papers.title: There are no unexpected toric positroid varieties
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a positroid. We prove that the positroid variety $\Pi_{\mathcal{M}}$ is toric with respect to some algebraic torus if and only if $\mathcal{M}$ is regular. In that case, $\Pi_{\mathcal{M}}$ is toric with respect to the standard diagonal torus. Thus, there are no unexpected toric positroid varieties.

papers.title: Toric Varieties from Multiple Zeta Values
papers.abstract: The linear relations among fixed weight multiple zeta values (MZVs) are a well-studied subject in number theory. Elements of putative linear bases for this fixed-weight space are, however, not algebraically independent; they satisfy non-linear relations. We study these relations by approximating them through motivic MZVs, formal MZVs and numerical computations. We show that motivic MZVs in fixed weight span a projective toric variety and explore its geometry. We define an outer approximation to the variety of formal MZVs in fixed weight by introducing toric varieties coming from shuffle and stuffle relations and taking their intersection. We conjecture that this intersection in fact agrees with the variety of formal MZVs and hence conjecturally also with the variety of motivic MZVs. This leads to a novel conjecture on a generating set for the extended double shuffle relations, which we checked computationally up to weight $23$.

papers.title: Tropical spin Hurwitz numbers
papers.abstract: We introduce a tropical framework for the study of spin Hurwitz numbers and their completed cycles analogues. We use degeneration techniques to obtain an interpretation of spin Hurwitz numbers via tropical covers. We employ the tropical methods to obtain new closed formulae for spin Hurwitz numbers in special cases. Moreover, we employ Fock space techniques to tropicalise completed cycles spin Hurwitz numbers. Using this, we prove that spin Hurwitz numbers admit a piecewise polynomial structure akin to their classical counterparts. We also derive wall--crossing formulae.

papers.title: Understanding Non-Split 2-Group Symmetry: (3+1)D SymTFT, Anomaly and Bordism
papers.abstract: We present a systematic study of finite, non-split 2-group symmetries with a non-trivial Postnikov class, focusing on the simplest example with a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ 0-form symmetry and a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ 1-form symmetry, intertwined together by the non-trivial Postnikov class in $H^3(B\mathbb{Z}_2;\mathbb{Z}_2)\cong\mathbb{Z}_2$, denoted by $\mathcal{G}$. We classify the anomalies of this 2-group symmetry for physical theories in $d$-dimensional spacetime, by computing the oriented bordism groups $\Omega_{d+1}^{\rm SO}(B\mathcal{G})$ and the spin bordism groups $\Omega_{d+1}^{\rm Spin}(B\mathcal{G})$ for $d\leq 5$. For the case of $d=3$, we investigate the Symmetry TFT/TO of the 2-group symmetry $\mathcal{G}$ using the language of fusion 2-categories, as well as (3+1)D TQFT actions, for the cases without or with the 2-group anomaly classified by $\operatorname{Hom}\left(\widetilde{\Omega}_4^{\rm SO}(B\mathcal{G}),U(1)\right) \cong H^4(B\mathcal{G};U(1))\cong\mathbb{Z}_2$. We classify the minimal topological and physical boundary conditions of the Symmetry TFTs, and carry out the categorical Landau paradigm for such a non-split finite 2-group.

papers.title: Uniform local models of quasi-unipotent $p$-adic differential equations
papers.abstract: We construct uniform analytic models of quasi-unipotent differential modules over Robba rings. For modules of rank at most $r$ and highest ramification break at most $b$, the inner radius of the model annulus depends only on $r,b$ and the residue characteristic $p$. At each radius, the model admits a basis, possibly depending on the radius, in which the connection matrix is bounded by a constant depending only on $r,b,p$. Both bounds are independent of the coefficient field, and these analytic models require no coefficient extension. A prescribed absolute Frobenius structure extends to such a bounded model with the same radius and connection bound. After a finite coefficient extension, we also realize quasi-constant modules, which carry the finite local monodromy, as differential direct summands of sums of pushforwards of rank-one modules, with uniformly bounded cover degrees and highest breaks of the inducing modules.

papers.title: Wavefront sets for genuine representations of $\rm GL$-covers of Kazhdan--Patterson or Savin types
papers.abstract: First, we consider general Brylinski--Deligne covers of the $p$-adic general linear groups, and discuss the theory of Bernstein--Zelevinsky derivatives. We also recall the Zelevinsky-type classification of the irreducible genuine spectrum for the Kazhdan--Patterson and Savin covers. Following this, for these two special families of covers, we determine the wavefront sets of their irreducible genuine representations, expressed in terms of the iterated degrees of the highest Bernstein--Zelevinsky derivatives. Finally, for Kazhdan--Patterson covers, we reinterpret this result on the wavefront set using a version of the local Langlands correspondence and the covering Barbasch--Vogan duality.

papers.title: When Polynomial Multiplication Counts Geometry: Schubert Polynomials and Monk's Rule
papers.abstract: We give a geometric introduction to Schubert polynomial multiplication through point-line flags in the complex projective plane. Moving a prescribed point onto a prescribed line gives a family with local equation $au=\lambda$, whose limiting curve has two components. The incidence equations and their local multiplicities give a two-term divisor product, using the standard intersection product on classes of algebraic cycles. Permutation labels and Schubert polynomials express the same decomposition as an instance of Monk's rule. For three incidence conditions, each allowing either a point on a prescribed line or a line through a prescribed point, the product has degree six. Under explicit general-position assumptions, direct construction and local equations give six distinct solutions of multiplicity one.

papers.title: Young's lattice, invariant ideals, and weak identities
papers.abstract: For a $d$-dimensional vector space $V$ over a field of characteristic zero, we show that $GL(V)$-stable ideals of the universal enveloping algebra of the free two-step nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak n_2(V)$ are in natural correspondence with filters in Young's lattice of integer partitions with at most $d$ rows. The same classification holds for $GL(V)$-stable Poisson ideals of $S(V\oplus\Lambda^2(V))$ with its natural Poisson bracket. As applications, we determine all weak polynomial identities of the $n$-th Weyl algebra relative to its standard generating subspace and of the universal enveloping algebra of the $(2n+1)$-dimensional Heisenberg Lie algebra relative to the Lie algebra itself.
